A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same kernel-regression explanation of in-context learning. Their complete main texts, equations, figures, and Appendices A–B support reliable comparison.

before.justification: Section 5 and Appendix B report original GPT-J experiments examining attention, prediction reconstruction, and information encoded in intermediate features.

after.justification: V2 retains these original experiments and adds reconstruction summaries and downstream comparisons in Section 5.5 and Tables 1–2.

M1.justification: The kernel weighting, label aggregation, attention interpretation, and feature-probing approach are retained. The new head-selection comparisons evaluate the existing reconstruction approach without establishing a revised model or learning algorithm.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate SST2, Rotten Tomatoes, MNLI, and Tweet Eval hate, irony, and offensive classification. All datasets appearing in the new tables were already represented in v1's main text or Appendix B.

E2.justification: V1 compares attention-based reconstructions with GPT-J predictions and ground-truth labels. V2 Table 2 substantially extends this comparison by adding kernel regression using all-MiniLM-L6-v2 and bert-base-nli-mean-tokens sentence encoders.

E3.justification: Section 5.5 introduces selection of an overall best head by average reconstruction accuracy across tasks, alongside task-specific selection. Existing experiments retain GPT-J-6B, SST2 validation data, 30-token attention alignment, and ridge regression with lambda 0.01.

E4.justification: The new comparison between task-specific best heads and one overall best head examines the effectiveness of using a common head across tasks. The original attention-location, similarity-correlation, and key/value probing analyses remain unchanged.

E5.justification: Neither version reports empirical repeated-run or seed counts, confidence intervals, or significance tests. The existing correlation analyses and reporting practices are retained.

E6.justification: Tables 1–2 add cross-task reconstruction summaries and downstream results for sentence-encoder and head-based kernels, substantially extending the reported comparisons. Existing figures remain unchanged. New values are not fully reconciled with retained results: Table 1 reports SST2 reconstruction accuracy of 0.864, whereas Section 5.2 still reports 89.2%.

T1.justification: V2 changes the assumptions, replacing the beginning-anchor condition with a delimiter-to-start-state condition, moving probability lower bounds into the formulation, and removing the margin-based task-deviation restriction. Theorem 1 replaces eventual argmax agreement with a posterior-vector approximation statement containing residual eta^2 epsilon_theta. Appendix A revises the derivation and corrects the undefined T^F quantity.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same central hypothesis: pretrained LLMs can implement kernel regression during ICL. The claimed attention/feature evidence and explanations of retrieval, label-format sensitivity, and demonstration distribution also remain.

C2.justification: V2 removes v1's explicit limitations concerning single-token classification and the simplicity of HMM language modeling, while retaining sample-order and perturbed-label challenges elsewhere. Section 5.5 additionally interprets the new performance comparisons as validating the kernels.

D1.justification: V2 adds resource links identifying the two sentence encoders but removes v1's promise to release code following publication. Existing hardware, model, attention-processing, and ridge-regression details remain unchanged.

R1.justification: New Section 2.3 discusses Chen and Li (2023) and Olsson et al. (2022), distinguishing their attention–kernel connections from this paper's setting and objectives. The previous literature coverage is otherwise retained.

P1.justification: V2 retitles the paper, makes grammatical edits, adds Sections 2.3 and 5.5, and removes the limitations section and acknowledgements. Most prose and the overall argument structure remain closely matched.

P2.justification: V2 adds two tables and changes the title, headers, and heading typography. All 20 original figures retain their content; appendix figures and headings are regrouped more consistently by dataset.

improvement.justification: V2 improves related-work coverage and repairs an undefined quantity and exposed draft comment in Appendix A. However, the new tables contain unreconciled SST2 values, and Appendix A does not justify the new little-o rate from its displayed square-root-order bound. Explicit single-token and HMM limitations also disappear. These technical and reporting issues leave the net benefit of the theoretical revision and added comparisons unclear.
